acceptance_criteria.statement: An element can carry exact code evidence, criterion and record links, saved documentation definitions and explicit inventory code selections; its separate reader actions open the corresponding saved content through the shared drawer or record page.
Changed code leaves the element stale in the reader, references, status and health until an author reassesses and edits its current explanation and pins; Git preserves previously committed evidence.

References and documented-code coverage attribute direct evidence and eligible explicit inventory selections from the current active board content to its stable element owner; historical Git content, unselected code and bare definition links do not add inherited coverage.

content.overview:
Whiteboard elements carry the semantic evidence and links that slide Items carry: pinned code, criterion and record links, exact technical-definition pins, and explicit inventory code selections. The element supplies its own geometry and reading context.

Changed code is a reason to reassess the design. Current documentation reports that debt; an author reads the changed code and edits the current complete document. Earlier committed content remains inspectable through Git at its original pins. A bare definition link does not acquire its code ownership, and a review deck retains independent changed-line coverage.
content.statement: As an architect, I can inspect a whiteboard element's exact code and related intent, and see when it needs reassessment, so the design remains trustworthy as the implementation changes.
content.title: Inspect and reassess whiteboard evidence

state.reason: Trevor explicitly requested Item-equivalent whiteboard evidence and mandatory stale-reference reassessment, then requested accepted product records for this completed capability. Acceptance records this confirmed intent; verification definitions and code evidence describe how it is checked.
